transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 09:00 PT
Duration: 34 minutes
Attendees: Ari Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (Redwood solutions eng - joined 10m in), Jared Cole (CTO - Stratus), Maya Lin (ML Eng), Omar Reyes (Infra), Priya Shah (PM)

Summary: quick sync to scope POC capacity and autoscale. Key goals: determine reserved GPU count, autoscale/burst plan, benchmark approach, and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ari: hey everyone, thanks for joining, real quick intros, i'm ari from redwood, im the AE on this deal. samira is our se for perf and infra.
[00:10] Jared: thanks, ari. yes i'm jared, cto at stratus. maya and omar and priya are here as well.
[00:16] Maya: hey all.
[00:18] Samira: thanks, quick agenda — confirm success criteria for the poc, size the reserved capacity, define autoscale thresholds and burst strategy, and agree benchmark plan. sound good?
[00:27] Omar: sounds good.
[00:28] Priya: yep.
[00:30] Ari: cool. to start, can you share the success criteria? what does a successful poc look like from your side?
[00:36] Jared: high level, we want to validate that redwood can meet our latency targets at production-ish traffic profiles and that unit cost is within our budget. also need to prove fallbacks — if primary model or capacity degrades we need graceful degradation.
[00:50] Priya: for product, we want 95th percentile under 350ms for short chat queries and 99th under 700ms for longer prompts, and for batch jobs we want throughput of at least 12k tokens/sec across our reserved pool.
[01:06] Maya: also verifying embedding pipelines — those run at higher qps but smaller token sizes, we want <50ms p95 for single embeddings.
[01:13] Samira: ok good, that gives concrete SLOs. what are your expected traffic patterns? avg rps, peak concurrency, tokens per request?
[01:20] Maya: typical bursty prodding — baseline 5 rps for chat, peak around 120 rps for short windows, median tokens per generation 80, worst case like 800 tokens for multi-turn summarization. embeddings are about 70 qps at peak, payloads 768 dims.
[01:36] Omar: and we expect 50 concurrent sessions hitting the model during peak, with some back-pressure on downstream services.
[01:42] Samira: helpful. on infra side, are you looking for dedicated GPUs for the poc or hosted with burst?
[01:49] Jared: leaning toward reserved GPUs to get predictable perf, but want burst capacity to handle peaks without overcommitting for the whole time. can you explain how redwood manages reserved vs burst?
[01:58] Ari: sure. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — you pick a commit for X GPUs for the POC window. we can configure a small reserved baseline (say 2x H100/A100 equivalents) and allow burst to a higher tier using a shared pool or on-demand nodes. burst is priced differently, and we can set autoscale policies for warm pools and cooldown to control churn.
[02:17] Samira: technically we route by model and latency policy, so during burst we can route low-latency requests to smaller quantized variants and reserve high-accuracy variants for lower-throughput paths as a fallback.
[02:28] Maya: sounds good. what's the cold start like for a new model variant? if we need to scale from 2 to 8 GPUs, how long until perf stabilizes?
[02:35] Samira: depends on model size and KV cache warmup; for a 70B model cold start to full readiness is around 20–45s to load weights and warm caches; for smaller 7–13B models it's under 15s typically. we also support pre-warmed standby replicas to reduce that to 3–8s, but that costs you reserved capacity.
[02:53] Omar: okay curious about kv cache — if the same user continues a conversation, will latency drop because of cache locality?
[02:58] Samira: yes, KV cache and prefix caching reduce token compute — for multi-turn chat you often see 30–60% token cost reduction after warmup. this affects how we size GPUs because cached workloads can handle more QPS per GPU.
[03:12] Jared: budget wise, what's your recommended reserved baseline for our profile? we mentioned median tokens 80, peaks 120 rps, some long jobs.
[03:20] Samira: rough ballpark — if you're running the 13B family at default FP16 quantization on A100-class, one GPU can handle ~1200–1800 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batching. for your baseline of steady 5 rps with median 80 tokens that's tiny; but peaks are the constraint. for 120 rps with median 80 tokens that's 9.6k tokens/sec, so i'd recommend reserved 4 GPUs baseline and autoscale up to 10 GPUs for bursts if you want headroom and minimal queuing.
[03:50] Luis: (joined) sorry for the slight delay, hey team. just to add, we often recommend starting with a slightly conservative reserved commit and rely on burst to cover traffic spikes while we run benchmarks to fine-tune.
[04:01] Priya: what about for the heavy long prompts, the 800 token cases — that changes perf dramatically right?
[04:06] Samira: yes, longer sequences reduce throughput. for 800-token requests throughput per GPU drops significantly, so we'll need to account for a small % of heavy requests in the autoscale algorithm, or direct those to a separate dedicated pool to avoid impacting short-chat latency.
[04:20] Maya: can we do model variants — like quantized 8-bit for burst and full precision for critical requests?
[04:24] Samira: yes, we support model variants: quantized / optimized kernels for high throughput and a higher-accuracy variant for quality-sensitive calls. you can route by route-tag or header or have automatic fallback on quality checks. downside is slight degradation in quality for quantized models; we'll want to run your eval set.
[04:39] Jared: about fallback policies, we need automatic graceful degradation: if a burst oversubscribes, we want to fallback to a smaller model or queue with informative retry headers. how's that configured?
[04:48] Samira: we have routing policies: fallback to compatible variants (e.g., 13B-quantized) with lower latency/throughput footprint, or degrade feature-level responses like shorten generation length. also we can return structured error + retry-after headers and rely on client-side backoff. we'll include demo of policy configs in the SOW.
[05:03] Omar: do you have recommended autoscale thresholds? like CPU/GPU util vs queued requests?
[05:09] Samira: we commonly use a hybrid rule: scale up when avg GPU utilization > 70% OR queue length > X (we use tokens pending / sec > threshold). scale down after utilization < 45% for a cooldown of 120s by default. you can tune cooldown to avoid flapping. for POC I recommend aggressive scale-up and conservative scale-down.
[05:26] Priya: how do burst costs look? we need to present a rough POC budget to finance.
[05:31] Ari: i'll send a POC pricing sheet but rough numbers: reserved GPUs billed at flat commit monthly pro-rata, burst billed per-minute with a premium ~1.8–2.5x of reserved per-minute cost depending on GPU type and region. we'll include an example spreadsheet for your traffic profile.
[05:46] Maya: security/regulatory note — we need logs, audit trails, and KMS support. will POC cover VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
[05:55] Ari: yes on VPC peering and KMS — for Redwood Private or a VPC-enabled Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS and provide audit logs. for the hosted POC we can also support VPC peering into staging. we'll attach SOC2 docs and the security pack.
[06:09] Jared: great. for benchmarks, what exactly will you run?
[06:13] Samira: plan: 1) synthetic perf pass to measure throughput on representative model sizes and sequence lengths, 2) run your prompt set and measure accuracy/loss/regression vs baseline, 3) run 2-hour soak with traffic mix and burst windows to observe autoscale behaviour. we'll share scripts and a test plan.
[06:29] Maya: will the soak include embeddings and generation together? that's our real-world mix.
[06:33] Samira: yes, we'll emulate mixed workloads including embeddings, short chat, and long summarizations.
[06:38] Omar: how long to stand up environment for benchmarks? staging access time?
[06:41] Samira: if you give staging VPC peering and network rules in 48 hours we can provision a test cluster in about 4–6 hours. otherwise we can run benchmarks in our hosted sandbox with mock data earlier.
[06:52] Jared: timeline — we'd like to complete POC and have decision by end of July. can you support a 2–3 week POC starting early July?
[06:59] Ari: yes that's doable. recommend the schedule: week of July 7 — initial benchmark and perf tuning; week of July 14 — production-scale soak and analytics; final week for runbook & decision.
[07:11] Priya: sounds good. can you outline the SOW items we will need for sign-off?
[07:15] Ari: SOW will include reserved GPU commit (count & type), burst allowance and pricing cap, benchmark plan, data handling & security terms, success criteria acceptance matrix, and timelines.
[07:26] Maya: on success criteria, define exact metrics we'll measure — p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, embedding p95, quality regressions threshold (like <2% MRR drop).
[07:36] Samira: yes we'll include quantitative thresholds and a script to compute them.
[07:40] Jared: question — if our on-prem infra needs to run the model, do you support private deployment for POC? we have some reg data.
[07:48] Samira: Redwood Private can be scoped but typically that adds setup time. for POC we usually do VPC peering or dedicated in a private region; private on-prem can be done but we'd treat it as a longer timeline, maybe months.
[08:01] Omar: one more infra question — will we be able to set autoscale min/max by route? e.g., keep embeddings in a small dedicated pool while chat autoscale separate?
[08:09] Samira: yes per-route policies supported. you can pin models and pools per route and set independent autoscale bounds and fallback policies.
[08:16] Maya: for evaluation we want to run quality comparisons between the quantized variant and the baseline. are there tooling hooks for diffing outputs?
[08:23] Samira: we'll run eval harnesses and produce comparison reports; we can also plug into your existing eval infra if you share the test suite.
[08:31] Priya: about monitoring — will we get per-token cost dashboards and tracing so we can see which prompts are expensive?
[08:36] Ari: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdown, cost, latency, and tracing with request IDs; we can enable retention for the POC.
[08:46] Jared: for fallback, can you do an automatic A/B where X% of traffic goes to high-accuracy variant and rest to throughput variant during bursts?
[08:54] Samira: yep, that's supported — traffic split policies, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback on regression. all that can be part of the POC runbook.
[09:03] Maya: curious about autoscale cooldown — you recommended 120s, is that adjustable? we worry about quick oscillations in bursts.
[09:09] Samira: totally adjustable. for bursty workloads we set longer cooldowns and larger scale steps to avoid thrash; also warm pools and pre-warm actions help.
[09:18] Omar: what about long job queueing — do you allow prioritized queues so batch summarization doesn't slow down chat?
[09:24] Samira: yes we have priority routing — you can reserve slots for high priority traffic and put batch jobs in lower priority with retry semantics.
[09:31] Jared: ok let's get practical — based on what you said, reserved 4 GPUs baseline, autoscale to 10 GPUs, with pre-warmed standby of 1–2 for faster cold starts. does that capture it?
[09:40] Samira: yes that's the initial recommendation. we'll validate with the benchmark and likely tune to 3–6 reserved depending on quantization and real-world cache hit rates.
[09:49] Ari: i'll include two SOW scenarios: conservative (4 reserved -> burst 10) and aggressive (6 reserved -> burst 12) with cost examples.
[09:57] Priya: for acceptance, we'll run the soak and check our SLOs and cost/cpu targets; if the POC meets SLOs and cost per 1k tokens is within target we accept.
[10:07] Maya: one more — data retention and logging, we need logs for 90 days and ability to redact PII.
[10:13] Ari: we can set retention and provide redaction tools; we'll include that in the security appendix.
[10:19] Jared: ok good. i'm comfortable with this plan. any blockers from redwood side?
[10:23] Samira: no blockers; just need your prompt set, staging network access (or opt for hosted sandbox) and to agree on SLO thresholds.
[10:31] Luis: i'll own the perf script and coordinate with maya on exact prompt formatting.
[10:35] Maya: great.
[10:37] Ari: recap of action items and next steps — i'll send POC SOW + pricing by Friday 2026-07-02, samira will deliver benchmark scripts and test plan by 2026-07-05, maya to upload prompt set by 2026-07-03, omar to confirm network details by 2026-07-06, schedule initial perf window week of 2026-07-07.
[10:55] Priya: sounds good.
[10:56] Jared: thanks everyone.
[10:58] Ari: thanks all, we'll follow up in calendar invite.

End of meeting.
